messages:
sara-support: FYI ACME reported a spike of 500s and timeouts this morning 09:12-09:22 UTC. They can't find a request id in their mobile logs. Can we give them a short checklist for (1) grabbing the request/trace id from our Console, (2) extracting it from their Android SDK logs, and (3) a curl that prints the response headers so they can forward a repro?

bob-support: +1. Also ask them to include the time window and customer project id. Without that it's hard to locate in our traces.

mike-eng: Quick checklist I usually paste: 
- Console: Project > Requests > set timeframe > click an entry > copy `Trace ID` from the header. If they see multiple entries, use the earliest 5xx.
- curl repro (prints response headers):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 2>&1 | sed -n '/< HTTP\//,$p'
```
Look for response headers: `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-request-id`. Ask them to paste that header value.

mike-eng: If the customer has a proxy (envoy/nginx) they can also grep access logs for our upstream header: `grep -i "x-redwood-request-id" /var/log/envoy/access.log | tail -n 50` — that'll show proxied requests with the header we set.

katie-devex: Short SDK tips to include for the customer: 
- JS/Node: set `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and watch console for `request_id=` lines.
- Android (SDK v1.4+): enable verbose logs: `Redwood.configure { logLevel = DEBUG }` then search logcat for `RedwoodRequestId:`. Example log line: `I/Redwood: request_id=01GZ... status=500 duration=412ms`.

jen-mobile: For Android repro, suggest they run this to capture logcat snippet while reproducing:
```
adb logcat -v time | grep Redwood | tee redwood-logs.txt
```
And include the redwood-logs.txt plus the exact request payload and timestamp.

sara-support: Nice. What about HAR / browser?

mike-eng: For browser flows: open DevTools > Network > reproduce > right-click the request > Save as HAR with content. They should send the HAR and mark the request. We look for `request.headers['x-request-id']` or our response header.

bob-support: Also remind them to redact any API keys before sending the HAR/logs. If they can provide a minimal curl (same request body) that reproduces the error we can replay it internally.

katie-devex: Minimal required to triage: `project_id`, `time_window` (UTC), `request_id/trace_id` (if available), HAR or curl output (with headers), SDK logs (redacted). If mobile, indicate OS version and SDK version.

sara-support: I'll DM customer the checklist. One more: can we ask infra to surface a quick grep helper in Console for `x-redwood-request-id`? :thinking_face:

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: `console-search:grep-helper` scheduled for staging deploy at 2026-05-12T03:00Z.

mike-eng: For now, if they can't find the header, ask them to set a client-generated header for repro: `X-Request-ID: my-local-test-123` and re-run. If we see that in our logs, we can follow it through the stack. :+1:

sara-support: Perfect — sending to ACME now. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
